subject: IP indemnity / liability cap — evidence request and proposed offset
messages:

Subject: Potential third-party patent notice — need carve-out path for IP indemnity

Aisha / Lauren —

Thanks for the recent drafts on the MSA and Order Form. We have a pending third-party notice that we need to disclose to our legal/procurement teams before finalizing the agreement. The short version: a vendor has contacted us alleging patent overlap with a feature in the analytics pipeline that would be covered by Redwood’s indemnity.

Helios’ procurement counsel is asking for a clear path so that (i) IP indemnity claims are not effectively immunized by a small monetary cap, and (ii) we have a defined evidence and notice process in the contract. Specifically, they are requesting either (A) a carve-out to the liability cap for IP indemnity (defense + damages) or (B) a separate, higher cap for IP-related claims tied to the orders.

Can you confirm Redwood’s position on (A) / (B) and what documentation you would need from Helios to evaluate? We’ve attached the initial notice we received for context. We’re trying to avoid escalation but procurement needs comfort to move forward.

Regards,
Jordan Miles
Director, Procurement — Helios Analytics
[Attachment: preliminary_notice_of_claim.pdf (PDF, 460KB)]

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the notice. I’ve looped in Marcus from legal and Lauren (who owns our order form) so we can triage this quickly. High-level: Redwood accepts that serious IP claims are different from run-of-the-mill service failures and we’re willing to negotiate narrowly tailored language to address Helios’ concerns.

To move efficiently, please confirm two things: 1) full copy of the notice (signed/dated), and 2) whether Helios seeks (A) an absolute carve-out to the liability cap for IP indemnity (i.e., IP claims excluded from the cap entirely) or (B) a separately quantified cap for IP claims tied to the annual contract value. We’ll also ask legal for a commercial compromise (e.g., limited carve-out + evidentiary gating).

Proposed next step: Marcus will propose redline language for the MSA and order form. If Helios can provide the notice PDF and any prior communications with the claimant, that will speed the evaluation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here — procurement timelines noted.

Best,
Aisha Rahman

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Potential third-party patent notice — need carve-out path for IP indemnity

Team —

I reviewed the preliminary notice. Quick thoughts and a proposed path forward below. I’ve attached a draft redline for the MSA (proposed_redline_MSA_Aisha_v2.pdf).

Summary position (commercial/legal balance):
- We will not agree to an open-ended carve-out that removes all monetary limits for IP claims. That creates disproportionate exposure.
- Redwood is willing to accept a limited IP indemnity carve-out that: (i) applies only to direct damages and reasonable defense costs for third-party IP claims, (ii) is triggered only after the customer provides a timely and complete notice plus the claimant’s notice, and (iii) is subject to an evidentiary review period.
- Optional commercial mitigations: escrow for awarded damages, or requiring customer to pursue mitigation with claimant before full indemnity; alternatively, set a higher fixed sub-cap for IP claims (e.g., 3x the annual fees) rather than removing the cap entirely.

Draft redline notes (attached):
- New IP carve-out clause: "Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), claims for third‑party intellectual property infringement shall be excluded from the monetary cap to the extent of direct damages and reasonable defense costs, provided that (a) Customer delivers written notice and claimant materials within 30 days of receipt; (b) Redwood’s liability shall be limited to the lesser of (i) actual direct damages and reasonable defense costs and (ii) three times Customer’s total fees for the 12 months preceding the claim unless customer elects escrow or insurance in lieu of an increased cap."
- Evidence gating: require claimant notice and allow Redwood 45 days to investigate before binding obligations accrue.

Please review the redline and let me know if we want the carve-out template to be (i) exclusion-from-cap OR (ii) elevated sub-cap. My instinct is to offer the elevated sub-cap as the commercial compromise.

- Marcus
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_redline_MSA_Aisha_v2.pdf]

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@integrilaw.com>
To: marcus@redwood.com, aisha@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@heliosanalytics.com>, Natalie Park <npark@heliosanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential third-party patent notice — need carve-out path for IP indemnity

Marcus / Aisha —

Thanks for the quick review. Attached is the formal notice Helios received (same as Jordan’s attachment) plus an outline from our side summarizing likely exposure. Helios’ position: an elevated sub‑cap is acceptable only if it covers defense costs and any injunctive remedies; otherwise Helios requires an exclusion from the limitation of liability for IP indemnity.

A few clarifications from our side:
1) Helios needs an explicit notification and cooperation process with Redwood for IP claims (who leads defense, settlement approvals).
2) If Redwood proposes escrow or insurance to limit recovery, Helios will consider it but requires guarantees on timing and coverage limits.
3) We can accept an elevated sub-cap if it is at least three (3) times annual fees and covers defense costs plus damages.

We’ll sign the updated order form once we have agreed text. I have attached the notice and our memo.

Elena Rossi
Partner, Integri Law (counsel to Helios Analytics)
[Attachment: preliminary_notice_of_claim.pdf, helios_infringement_memo.pdf]

From: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@heliosanalytics.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, marcus@redwood.com
Cc: Natalie Park <npark@heliosanalytics.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@integrilaw.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential third-party patent notice — proposed commercial compromise and next steps

Jordan / Elena / Natalie —

Appreciate the details and the memo. Based on Marcus’ redline and your feedback, Redwood can accept the following commercial compromise to close the item and keep the procurement timeline intact:

1) IP carve-out limited to direct damages and reasonable defense costs for third‑party IP claims; carve-out will be implemented as an elevated sub‑cap equal to three (3) times Helios’ annual fees (measured over the prior 12 months).
2) The carve-out covers defense costs and monetary damages but does not expand remedial obligations beyond indemnity (i.e., Redwood will not be required to provide injunctive relief).
3) Evidence & timing: Helios must deliver the claimant notice and supporting materials within 30 days of receipt; Redwood will have 45 days to complete initial investigation and confirm coverage.
4) Optional mitigation: if Helios prefers, Redwood will accept an escrow arrangement for awarded damages in lieu of increasing the cap; customer to propose escrow agent and funding schedule.

I’ve uploaded the redline that incorporates the above and a DocuSign order form for signature. If Helios accepts the elevated sub‑cap approach, we can finalize today. If you prefer the exclusion route, Marcus has flagged that we’ll need additional underwriting/insurance.

Next steps: Natalie — if procurement signs off, we’ll route the redline through DocuSign (link below). Marcus — please review the attached final redline and confirm we’re comfortable with the settlement/defense approvals language before sending to Elena to insert any counsel edits.

Draft attachments: proposed_redline_MSA_Aisha_v2.pdf; docusign_orderform_helios_link.txt

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
